caption:
Same business. Different structure. The tax gap can hit 5 figures.

Sole trader: every dollar of profit is taxed at your marginal rate. Above $190,000 in 2026–27 that's 45% plus 2% Medicare levy. Simple to run, no corporate admin, but no rate cap.

Base rate entity company: 25% flat rate on taxable income (turnover under $50M, passive income 80% or less, 2026–27). Lower rate — but profit taxed in the company isn't the same as money in your pocket. To get it out, you pay dividends (franking credits offset personal tax). And Division 7A is a real risk if you use company money personally without the right structure.

When the switch makes financial sense:
- Your effective marginal rate significantly exceeds 25%
- Profits genuinely stay in the business (reinvestment, retained earnings)
- The gap covers the costs of set-up, an annual accountant, and company compliance

The structure also affects asset protection, succession, and how you pay yourself — there's no one right answer. Worth paying a registered adviser to model it for your numbers.

Are you a sole trader thinking about structuring? What's the question you can't get a straight answer to?
